craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of criterion; vyabhicāri exultation at awareness uncontainable. Sanskrit-first: jaḍa (INERT — kept technical, not ‘unconscious’); aprameya (UNMEASURABLE — passive kept: cannot-be-measured). Rows: 1 (‘measured’ closes — what awareness escapes, named last), 9 (in-part vs stands-apart echo), 5 (criterion tread: mark L1, difference L2). Close: ‘it cannot be measured’. Rupture: semicolon (mark turns to difference). Rejected: ‘the unconscious’ — killed: technical kept; ‘transcends measure’ — killed: passive kept; ‘fragmentary’ for ‘in part’ — killed: ekadeśa kept plain. Read aloud: TO-shine ON-ly IN-part — THAT is the MARK of the in-ERT … a-WARE-ness STANDS a-PART … FOR it CAN-not BE-mea-SURED.

lines: To shine only in part — that is the mark of the inert;
awareness stands apart from the inert, for it cannot be measured.
l4.sanskrit_cite: paricchinnaprakāśatvaṃ jaḍasya kila lakṣaṇam | jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate

reads_against.argmap: How is awareness told apart from the inert? → Mark then difference: partial shining vs measure-evading awareness.
c1_essence: Partial shining marks inert; measure-evading awareness differs.
